payload.title: The ARIA-HISTORICAL, ARIA-SUPERSEDED and ARIA-LIVE-AUTHORITY header markers have two owners that disagree on where a marker counts: the adapter reads them in the first 5 lines only, the invariant spec counts them anywhere in the body, and no test relates the two lists
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:344-345 (RECORD_MARKERS lists two of the markers and MARKER_HEAD_LINES is 5)
tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:384-388 (the live-authority banner is a third spelling with its own regex and the same 5-line window)
tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:403-404 (the marker test slices the first 5 lines)
tests/invariants/aria-doc-runtime-ssot.spec.ts:189-194 (planMarkerCount counts occurrences anywhere in the document body)
tests/invariants/aria-doc-runtime-ssot.spec.ts:263-269 (every ARIA plan document must hold exactly one marker, at any position)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md single-owner principle (every concept has one owner; a second copy is deleted or pinned by an invariant).
payload.notes: A docs/aria/plans document that carries its single ARIA-HISTORICAL marker on line 7 satisfies the invariant (one marker, anywhere), yet isPointInTimeRecord returns false for it (probe at a81bfa2d6), so the adapter scans the plan as live and emits its missing references as stale claims. A new marker added to PLAN_MARKERS is likewise invisible to the adapter. Not reachable today: every marker-carrying document under docs/aria, docs/adr/033 and docs/runbooks/aria-gateway.md holds it on line 1. Close condition: Export the marker words and the head window from the adapter (or a shared module) and make the invariant spec import them for PLAN_MARKERS, with an assertion that every docs/aria/plans document carries its marker inside that window; proof is the invariant failing when a marker is moved to line 6. Verified at origin/main a81bfa2d6.
